QuestionStmt.S: When an observer moves towards a stationary source with velocity '$V_1$', the apparent frequency of emitted note is '$F_1$'. When observer moves away from stationary source with velocity '$V_1$' the apparent frequency is '$F_2$'. If '$v$' is velocity of sound in air and $\frac{F_1}{F_2} = 2$, then $\frac{v}{V_1}$ is equal to

Solution.S:
Let the actual frequency of the source be $f$.

Case 1: Observer moves towards stationary source:
$$F_1 = f \left( \frac{v + V_1}{v} \right)$$

Case 2: Observer moves away from stationary source:
$$F_2 = f \left( \frac{v - V_1}{v} \right)$$

Given $\frac{F_1}{F_2} = 2$:
$$\frac{\frac{v + V_1}{v}}{\frac{v - V_1}{v}} = 2 \Rightarrow \frac{v + V_1}{v - V_1} = 2$$

Cross-multiplying:
$$v + V_1 = 2(v - V_1)$$
$$v + V_1 = 2v - 2V_1$$
$$v + V_1 - 2v + 2V_1 = 0$$
$$-v + 3V_1 = 0$$
$$v = 3V_1$$

Thus $\frac{v}{V_1} = 3$, which corresponds to option C.
